ai.literal: The end of deliberation is attaining resolution; that resolution lingering in delay is harmful.
ai.translation: The end of deliberation is to arrive at a firm resolution; but for that resolution to linger in delay is harmful.
ai.modern: ஆராய்ச்சியின் முடிவு ஒரு தெளிவான முடிவை அடைவதாகும்; அவ்வாறு எடுத்த முடிவு செயலில் இறங்காமல் காலதாமதத்தில் தங்கிவிடுவது தீமையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the transition from planning to action. The ultimate goal of any deliberation (சூழ்ச்சி) is to arrive at a firm, unwavering decision (துணிவு). However, once a decision has been reached, allowing that resolution to linger in procrastination or delay (தாழ்ச்சி) is highly detrimental. Hesitation after planning defeats the purpose of the initial analysis and leads to failure.

ai.literal: Delay, by delaying, those actions that are of the nature of being delayed; do not delay actions that are to be done without delaying.
ai.translation: Delay those actions that are fit to be delayed; but do not delay those actions that must be performed without delay.
ai.modern: நிதானமாகச் செய்ய வேண்டிய செயல்களைத் தாமதித்துச் செய்ய வேண்டும்; ஆனால், தாமதமின்றிச் செய்ய வேண்டிய செயல்களைத் தாமதிக்காமல் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of timing and pace in executing tasks. The verb 'tūṅku' literally means to hang or sleep, but here it is used in the sense of delaying or acting slowly and deliberately. The author advises that deeds requiring deep deliberation and patience should indeed be delayed and handled slowly. Conversely, deeds that demand swiftness and immediate attention must be executed without any hesitation or delay.

ai.literal: In all possible ways, action is indeed good; when not possible, having considered the way it will succeed, to do.
ai.translation: In every possible way, performing an action is good; if it is not possible, one should find a viable path to success and then act.
ai.modern: இயலும் வழிகளிலெல்லாம் செயலைச் செய்வது நல்லது; இயலாதபோது, அது வெற்றியடையும் வழியை ஆராய்ந்து செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises on the execution of tasks under different circumstances. In all situations where it is possible (ஒல்லும் வாய் எல்லாம்), performing the action directly is highly beneficial. However, when direct execution is not possible (ஒல்லாக்கால்), one must carefully analyze and find an alternative path or method that will lead to success (செல்லும்வாய் நோக்கி) and then proceed to act (செயல்). The key words 'ஒல்லும் வாய்' (possible ways) and 'செல்லும் வாய்' (viable paths of success) contrast the direct approach with the strategic, adaptive approach. Note: 'ஙல்லும்' is a variant/scribal representation of 'ஒல்லும்' in this context.

ai.literal: The remnant of the two called action and enmity, when considered, like the remnant of fire, will destroy.
ai.translation: When one considers them, the unfinished remnants of an action or an enmity will destroy a person, just like a remnant of fire left unextinguished.
ai.modern: செயல், பகை ஆகிய இரண்டின் எஞ்சிய பகுதி, ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்தால், அணையாமல் விடப்பட்ட நெருப்பின் எஞ்சிய பகுதி போல அழிவை உண்டாக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against leaving any task or enmity incomplete. The poet compares the remnants of an unfinished action (வினை) and an unresolved enmity (பகை) to a spark of fire (தீ) that is not fully put out. Just as a tiny leftover ember can flare up and burn down an entire house, any unfinished portion of a task or a lingering trace of hostility will eventually grow and destroy the person who neglected it. Therefore, both work and enmity must be resolved completely without leaving any residue.

ai.literal: Resources, instrument, time, action, along with place—all five, darkness being cleared, having analyzed, to act.
ai.translation: Analyze these five factors thoroughly until all doubts are cleared before embarking on an action: the required resources, the proper instruments, the right time, the nature of the action, and the suitable place.
ai.modern: தேவையான பொருள், தகுந்த கருவி, ஏற்ற காலம், செய்ய வேண்டிய செயல், அதற்குரிய இடம் ஆகிய ஐந்தையும் ஐயமற ஆராய்ந்து ஒரு செயலைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the five essential prerequisites for executing any task successfully. The five factors are the necessary resources (poruḷ), the appropriate tools or instruments (karuvi), the right timing (kālam), the nature of the deed itself (viṉai), and the proper location (iṭam). The phrase 'iruḷ tīra' (darkness being cleared) metaphorically refers to dispelling all doubts and ignorance. The poet advises that one must analyze all five elements with absolute clarity before initiating any action.

ai.literal: And the completion, and the obstacles, and the resulting benefit that will accrue there upon completion, having examined, one should do.
ai.translation: An action should be undertaken only after carefully considering the effort required for its completion, the obstacles that may arise, and the ultimate benefit that will be gained.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலை முடிப்பதற்கு ஆகும் முயற்சியையும், இடையில் வரும் இடையூறுகளையும், அது முடிந்த பிறகு கிடைக்கும் பயனையும் ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்து அச்செயலைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines three essential factors that must be analyzed before starting any undertaking. First, 'mutivu' refers to the final completion of the task and the resources or effort required to achieve it. Second, 'itaiyuru' represents the potential hindrances or difficulties that might arise along the way. Third, 'patupayan' is the actual profit or utility that will be realized once the task is finished. A wise person weighs all three aspects thoroughly before acting.

ai.literal: The method of acting of him who performs an action, is to win over the mind of him who knows the inner secrets of that action.
ai.translation: The way for one to successfully perform a task is to win over the mind of the person who knows the inner secrets of that task.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்ய விரும்புகிறவர் அச்செயலை வெற்றிகரமாக முடிக்கும் வழியாகக் கொள்ள வேண்டியது, அச்செயலின் நுட்பங்களை அறிந்தவருடைய மனத்தைக் கவர்ந்து தன்வசப்படுத்துவதே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the strategic approach to executing any task. The key to success for a doer (செய்வான்) lies in the method of action (செயன்முறை). Rather than working blindly, the doer must identify someone who already knows the inner secrets and complexities (உள்ளறிவான்) of that specific task (அவ்வினை). By winning over their mind and securing their goodwill (உள்ளம் கொளல்), the doer gains invaluable guidance and ensures the task is completed smoothly.

ai.literal: By one action, accomplishing another action and securing it, is like binding an elephant with a wet-templed elephant.
ai.translation: Accomplishing one task by means of another is like tethering a wild elephant using a strong, tame elephant.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைக் கொண்டு மற்றொரு செயலையும் செய்து முடித்துக் கொள்வது, மதநீர் ஒழுகும் கன்னத்தை உடைய ஒரு யானையைக் கொண்டு மற்றொரு யானையைக் கட்டுவதைப் போன்றது ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the art of multitasking and efficiency using a vivid simile. In ancient times, a strong, trained elephant (often in musth, indicated by its wet temples) was used to lure and capture wild elephants. Similarly, a wise person uses the momentum, resources, or execution of one ongoing action to accomplish another related task. This saves effort and doubles efficiency, turning one endeavor into a tool for another.

ai.literal: Than doing good things to friends, more urgent indeed is securing by allying those who are estranged.
ai.translation: Even more urgent than doing good to one's friends is to win over and ally with those who are estranged.
ai.modern: நண்பர்களுக்கு நன்மைகளைச் செய்வதை விட, பகைவர்களை நம்முடன் சேர்த்துக் கொள்வது மிகவும் அவசரமான செயலாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines a vital strategy in the execution of any major undertaking. While performing helpful deeds for existing friends is valuable, neutralizing opposition is a far more pressing priority. The word 'oṭṭār' refers to those who are estranged, hostile, or unaligned. By winning them over ('oṭṭi koḷal') and turning them into allies, one removes potential obstacles and secures a smoother path to success.

ai.literal: Fearing the inner trembling of those whose refuge is small, if their objective is obtained, the great will accept it, bowing humbly.
ai.translation: Fearing the inner terror of those with weak defenses, great leaders will accept their objective and make peace, even by acting with humility.
ai.modern: பாதுகாப்பு குறைந்த எளியவர்கள் மனநடுங்குவதை அஞ்சி, தங்களுக்கு வேண்டிய காரியம் நிறைவேறினால், பெரியவர்கள் பணிவுடன் நடந்து அதை ஏற்றுக் கொள்வார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the strategic humility of great leaders when dealing with weaker adversaries. Great statesmen do not seek to utterly terrify or destroy those who have weak defenses ('uṟai ciṟiyār'). Fearing the inner trembling ('uḷ naṭuṅkal añci') that extreme terror might cause in the weak—which could drive them to desperate, unpredictable actions—the great will gladly accept their objective ('kuṟai peṟiṉ') and conclude the matter, even by humbling themselves ('paṇintu koḷvar') to ensure a peaceful resolution.
